title: Session-tiered output-floor experiment + enterprise SQ onboarding playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Validate a session-tiered output-weighted minimum (OTM) that reduces bill volatility for conversational customers while preserving unit economics and enabling a smoother path for enterprise security questionnaire (SQ) commitments.

Background: Customers have complicated usage patterns — short bursty sessions and long-running sessions with heavy output token ratios (e.g., summarization, export). Existing directional IO minimums and streaming floors penalize some enterprise patterns and complicate SQ negotiations. We need an experiment that: (1) differentiates short vs long sessions, (2) weights minimums by output-heavy sessions, and (3) produces metrics and legal/SQ artifacts to accelerate enterprise commitments.

Hypothesis: Applying a session-length bucket and output-weight multiplier (session-tiered OTM) will: (a) increase predictable revenue from mid-sized customers by 12–20% on committed plans, (b) reduce customer support tickets about unexpected bills by 30%, and (c) have negligible negative churn impact on low-usage freemium power users.

Experiment design:
- Definition of session: contiguous websocket/HTTP streaming session where idle gap < 60s.
- Buckets:
  - Micro (session <= 30s): floor multiplier 0.25x base output-minimum
  - Standard (31s–5min): floor multiplier 1.0x
  - Heavy (5min–60min): floor multiplier 1.5x
  - Long-running (>60min): floor multiplier 2.0x and capped monthly credit rules
- Calculation: for each session compute output_tokens * bucket_multiplier = session-weighted-output. Bill applied across the billing period: max(existing per-direction floor, sum(session-weighted-output) across period).
- Streaming variant: real-time tagging for sessions created in streaming mode to ensure streaming-specific multipliers (e.g., micro-stream discount to avoid penalizing handshake-only streams).

Telemetry & success metrics:
- Primary metrics: change in monthly committed revenue (revenue delta), % of customers hitting the floor, median bill variance (month-over-month), and support tickets referencing 'unexpected bill' or 'floor'.
- Safety checks: increase in average invoice for bottom 40% of customers should be <= 10% unless proactively alerted/opted-in.
- Statistical plan: 2-sided test at 95% CI, power 0.8; A/B with 10k orgs in test and 10k in control for 8 weeks.

Operationalization & rollout:
- Instrumentation: billing pipeline flags per-session-weighted-output; incremental billing preview job will run during pilot weeks 1–4 with invoice mockups sent to selected customers.
- GTM: Sales/Solutions will get playbook snippets and a contract clause template explaining the session-tiered floor and examples on two customer archetypes.
- Support: FAQ and escalation runbook; dedicated Slack channel #pricing-otm-pilot.

Security & enterprise SQ onboarding:
- Requirement: all pricing changes that modify meter calculation must be documented in the customer-facing SQ appendix and in the legal pricing exhibit (for enterprise SOWs).
- Deliverables for SQ: updated pricing exhibit language, telemetry proof-of-behavior screenshots, and a one-page security note explaining that no customer payload is used for pricing decisions and that KMS/HSM and audit logs are unaffected.
- Security review required: yes (see security_review_required field).

Acceptance criteria for full rollout:
- Pilot achieves target revenue delta or provides clear tradeoffs documented for executive decision.
- No more than 10 escalations with billing-impact severity > P2.
- Legal approves exhibit language and Sales confirms 3 pilot customers willing to sign with new language.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Long-running sessions (e.g., batch export) unexpectedly push bills for low-traffic enterprises. Mitigation: monthly cap and opt-in grace period plus invoice preview.
- Risk: Complexity increases support load. Mitigation: automated FAQ + real-time invoice preview + proactive email communications during pilot.
